security_spec.violation_condition: When a vCPU executes in VS-mode or VU-mode (env->virt_enabled == true) and directly encodes vsiselect (0x250) or any vsireg* (0x251–0x257) CSR number in a CSR instruction, QEMU's predicate functions csrind_hmode() and csrind_or_aia_hmode() guard only on extension presence (ext_smcsrind/ext_sscsrind) and RVH existence, but never check env->virt_enabled. The spec's norm:sscsrind_virtual_inst_fault requires a virtual-instruction exception for any direct VS/VU-mode access to these CSRs. Additionally, the rmw_xiselect() and rmw_xireg() paths check only mstateen0[60] via smstateen_acc_ok(env, 0, SMSTATEEN0_SVSLCT) but never consult hstateen0[60] for VS/VU-mode access to siselect/sireg*, violating norm:hypervisor_impl_csrs_access_control which requires a virtual-instruction exception when hstateen0[60]=0 even if mstateen0[60]=1.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: static RISCVException csrind_hmode\(|static RISCVException csrind_or_aia_hmode\(.*\n.*\n.*return hmode\(|smstateen_acc_ok\(env, 0, SMSTATEEN0_SVSLCT\)
security_spec.summary: csrind_hmode/csrind_or_aia_hmode predicates lack env->virt_enabled guard allowing VS/VU-mode direct access to vsiselect/vsireg* without the mandatory virtual-instruction fault; additionally hstateen0[60] is never checked for siselect/sireg* access, letting guests bypass hypervisor disable of indirect CSR access
